text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan, is set to leave office on Wednesday because of public pressure.
- The chairman of an exporters group says nothing has changed in economic terms from a year earlier because the government has pursued populist policies.
MILLIYET

- A court freezes over $100 million worth of accounts and securities belonging to a leading Islamist group of companies after military claims that Islamic businessmen were supporting religious activism.
- Erbakan persuades a far-right party to become the third partner in a planned caretaker government in an attempt to push through an early polls plan.
HURRIYET
- The conservative wing of the coalition threatens to pull out of the Islamist-led governement if Erbakan does not submit his resignation to President Suleyman Demirel by midnight.
- The constitutional court gives Erbakan's Welfare Party one month to submit a written defence against a case aimed at forcing the party's closure.
YENI YUZYIL
- Speculation heightens over who President Demirel is to appoint as prime minister if Erbakan goes ahead with his expected resignation.
- Parliament will reconsider a draft law requiring the closure of casinos after Demirel vetoed the plan.
CUMHURIYET
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz tries to form an alternative government to frustrate plans for a three-way coalition including the two existing alliance partners.
DUNYA
- Koc Holding is planning to sell 15 percent of the dairy products company SEK to the French company Candy.
- A trade union leader says Turkey's 1997 revenue from tourism is expected to amount to $7.5 billion.
ZAMAN
- The interior ministry asks for some mosques and Koran teaching centres to be monitored for any statements against the founder of modern Turkey, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk and the secularist army.
